findings.summary: Policy mutation trusts caller-supplied role instead of authoritative workspace authorization.
findings.details: The task requires existing workspace role resolution to remain authoritative and policy changes to be limited to org admins/owners. bulkSetChannelPolicies exposes actorRole as an argument and forwards it to the planner; an internal caller can claim admin/owner for an organization without the mutation resolving the actor membership or role.

findings.summary: Persisted policy changes do not move a single active immutable policy pointer.
findings.details: The implementation never reads existing routing or delivery policies, so every persisted policy computes epoch/generation 1. It also only inserts active=true rows and never deactivates prior active rows. This breaks the lifecycle requirement that rollback/change creates a new immutable epoch while moving the active pointer after validation.

findings.summary: Channel-level generation fencing is missing for concurrent directory races.
findings.details: The task explicitly requires stale connection/channel generation changes to fail. The public mutation contract includes only expectedConnectionGeneration, and the planner checks only SourceChannelRow.connectionGeneration. It ignores SourceChannelRow.accessGeneration, so a policy request based on stale channel membership/access state can be accepted after a concurrent directory reconciliation changes the channel generation.

findings.summary: Bulk policy mutation is not replay/idempotency safe.
findings.details: Accepted policy requests have no idempotency key or expected prior epoch and every invocation inserts new routing and delivery rows. Retrying the same mutation after an ambiguous client/server failure can append duplicate active policy rows and duplicate side effects rather than deterministically returning the already-applied result.

findings.summary: Real capability cannot detect the 101st active channel because it truncates before validation.
findings.details: The pure planner rejects more than 100 active joined channels only when it receives more than 100 rows, but the mutation reads sourceChannels with take(100). If an organization has 101 active joined channels, the implementation supplies at most 100 rows to the planner and can accept a policy instead of enforcing the launch envelope.
